**God's Eye // UAP 2.0: NASA's bright fireballs on the globe and in every sighting check, a compass and tilt for the view, and two more tools for AI assistants.**

### ▶ [Open the live app](https://domw99.github.io/Gods-Eye-UAPs/)

**Fireballs**
- **A new layer** with the 888 bright meteors that U.S. government sensors have recorded since 1988 (NASA's Center for Near Earth Object Studies, public domain), drawn as comets sized by their energy. Click one for its time, place, energy (as tons or kilotons of TNT), height and speed. The years bar filters them. Chelyabinsk, 15 February 2013, is the big one: about 440 kt.
- **Every case since 1988** now has a *Bright fireballs nearby* section: any fireball in the record within 600 km and 3 hours (12 hours when the case's time of day is approximate), with how long before or after, how far and in which direction. A fireball outshines the Moon for a few seconds and is a familiar cause of "a light that crossed the sky and went out". None of the 46 cases since 1988 has one, and the section says so; it also says the record holds only the bigger events, so an empty answer does not rule one out.
- **What did I see?** adds the fireball as a candidate: strong for a fast light seen minutes from one, weak for a light that stood still.
- The data is built into the app (NASA's API does not allow requests from a web page), refreshed monthly by the same workflow as the Kp index, and works offline.

**The view**
- **A compass** that turns with the view, and **north up** (button or <kbd>B</kbd>) that turns it back by the short way, about the middle of the screen.
- **Tilt** (button or <kbd>P</kbd>) leans the view 45° to see the ground from an angle, and brings it back to straight down. High above the Earth there is nothing to lean over, so it asks you to zoom in first.

**For AI assistants**
- The MCP server has two more tools: `fireballs_near` (the record near a place and time) and `globe_link` (a link that opens the globe on a case or a place with layers on, with the case's page and an embed address). `?layers=fireballs` works in any link.

**Behind it**
- Looked at the other God's Eye projects again: upstream's changes since 1.9 are mostly live feeds, API keys and voice, which this keyless static app does not take. What fitted was the tilt and north-up control, and its way of handing a view to an assistant as a link. YOGART, a UAP research map, supplied the fireball idea.
- 1,118 unit tests and the browser tests, with new ones for the layer, the case section, the checker, the compass and the two tools; 40 new texts in all 15 languages.
